## Analysis

**Note on frame fidelity:** The character is small (~60–80 px tall at the right edge of frame) and rendered nearly black against a dark background, so all angles below are estimates with ±10° confidence. Both frames also show the character near-idle/standing rather than mid-stride, which limits how much "sprint dynamics" can actually be verified.

### (1) Sprint posture — **Fails / not readable as a sprint**
- Trunk lean in Image 1 reads as roughly **10–15° forward at most**, likely less — the torso looks nearly vertical. This is below the 20–35° max-velocity window.
- **No heel-to-butt recovery is visible.** Both legs appear relatively extended/straight beneath the hips; there's no high rear heel or folded recovery leg. It reads more as a stand/walk-cycle frame than a sprint.
- Gaze direction can't be confirmed (the head is ~5 px of dark pixels with a cyan eye-glint), so "level gaze" is unverifiable.
- Verdict: this does not read as a max-velocity sprinter posture.

### (2) Dash vs. sprint contrast — **Fails**
- Image 2's trunk lean is roughly **5–15°, essentially the same as or even slightly more upright than** Image 1. There is no 45°+ acceleration lunge.
- No "power line" from rear toe through hips to crown: the hip is stacked over/near the feet rather than trailing behind, and the extended leg drives *down/forward along the blade swing*, not back.
- The pose difference between the two frames is dominated by the **arm/blade swing** (blade raised high in Image 1, swept down-forward in Image 2), not by whole-body acceleration lean. A dash should read through the spine angle first; here it doesn't.

### (3) Silhouette readability — **Poor to marginal**
- The **blade** is clearly readable (bright gold/yellow highlight — the highest-contrast element, which is good).
- The **head/eye** reads via the cyan glint.
- The **arms and legs** are very difficult to distinguish: dark limbs on dark background with no rim light. In Image 1, a thin arm with a small ring/pommel detail trails left of the body but reads as a wire, not a limb. Legs blend into the character's cape/coat mass.
- Recommendation: add a subtle rim-light or lighten limb strokes ~20–30% so limbs separate from the torso silhouette.

### (4) Arm proportions — **Suspect / hard to verify**
- The visible trailing arm appears **long and thin**, with the forearm possibly longer than the upper arm (the elbow kink is barely visible). The tiny ring at the end suggests the hand, but the reach looks slightly overlong for the torso height (arm span appears > 1× torso length, which is borderline).
- The blade-side arm is completely occluded by the weapon and torso, so elbow bend is unreadable. Can't confirm correct 1:1 upper/forearm ratio with confidence — but nothing screams "broken."

### (5) Broken limbs / artifacts — **None catastrophic, one ambiguity**
- No obviously inverted knee/elbow (no backward-bending joint is discernible).
- The trailing arm's small circle (pommel/ring?) floats ambiguously — it could be misread as a detached hand or an artifact at this size.
- The blade's reflection in the floor is present and consistent; no double-limb or z-order glitch visible.
- The cape/coat shape merges with the legs, which occasionally makes the lower body read as a single blob rather than two legs.

### Summary
| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Sprint posture (20–35° lean, heel recovery) | ❌ ~10–15° lean, no recovery fold |
| Dash more leaned than sprint (45°+) | ❌ No meaningful lean delta |
| Silhouette readability | ⚠️ Blade/head yes; limbs no |
| Arm proportions | ⚠️ Possibly overlong; elbow unreadable |
| Broken limbs/artifacts | ✅ None major; ambiguous hand-ring |

**Biggest fixes:** (a) push dash trunk lean to 40–55° with rear leg trailing, (b) exaggerate sprint heel recovery and add ~25° lean, (c) rim-light the limbs so the skeleton reads against the dark city backdrop.
message.reasoning_content: Analyze the two frames. Character small at right side. Image 1: standing fairly upright holding large blade diagonally; Image 2: blade swung down/lower. Both poses look fairly upright — dash doesn't read as deeply leaned. Provide quantitative estimates with caveats.
